decisions.reason: The Definition allowed any primal/dual edge path to be called open, including a face-boundary loop with w_0=w_n and zero boundary. This is a genuine terminology defect: over F_2, the telescoping boundary w_0+w_n is nonzero exactly when the endpoints differ. It is nonfatal because no invalid endpoint conclusion follows in the current consumers: ex-qsmx-toric-defect-pair explicitly requires distinct endpoint vertices/faces, while closed-string arguments require zero boundary. Both open-path clauses now require distinct endpoints; the same Pauli formulas remain explicitly available for closed paths.

reviews.reason: Checked the current complete Definition and its three actual prerequisite definitions. Finite q=2 spin factors, boundaryless manifold and integral-orientation conventions agree with those suppliers. Edge-chain boundaries telescope even with repeated edges or loops; distinct endpoints therefore separate open paths from zero-boundary closed paths in either graph. The explicit closed-path sentence preserves the closed-string operator interface. Mod-two incidence, commuting Pauli involutions, positive penalties, coordinate crossings and support conventions are unchanged. No physical premise or empirical claim is introduced, and this item has no diagram or proof to stamp. This is the adjudicator's repair review, not an independent review of that repair.
